summary: Adversarial probe of apps/api/src/core/guards/billing-enforcement.guard.ts's blanket-deny-except-ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES model (normalizePath/startsWithAny). Confirmed with live Express instances (raw http.request, bypassing any client-side URL normalization) that the guard's own boundary check and the actual Nest/Express router always see the identical undecoded req.originalUrl string, so the classic double-slash (/billing//../artists/1/delete -> 404, not routed), dot-segment traversal (/billing/../artists/1/delete -> 404 with a raw socket request), percent-encoded-slash (/billing%2F..%2Fartists/1/delete -> 404) and substring-prefix-collision (startsWithAny's path===prefix||path.startsWith(prefix+'/') boundary check correctly rejects e.g. /support-requests against the '/support' entry; verified against the full @Controller() registry, no controller path collides) classes of attack do NOT let a request for a normally-blocked route slip through the allowlist while still being routed to its real (non-exempt) controller -- no fail-open bypass reproduced. However two real defects were found and filed: (1) find-cf172810 LOW: startsWithAny is case-sensitive but Express's default router is case-insensitive (verified empirically: GET /BILLING/portal actually routes 200 to the real billing controller) -- this fails CLOSED (wrongly blocks a suspended tenant's own path to pay via /billing on a differently-cased request), not a bypass, but undermines the allowlist's purpose. (2) find-9e311421 MEDIUM, pre-existing/inherited by the new logic: getState()/readStateRaw() return null (fail-open, 'if(!state) return true') indistinguishably for 'tenant never billed' and 'DataSource unavailable', so any DB/DI degradation silently disables enforcement for every tenant including suspended ones. ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES content itself was checked against every @Controller() route: '/billing' also exempts super_admin-only cross-tenant admin endpoints (suspend/reactivate/override/list-all-tenants) but those remain gated by an independent RequireRole('super_admin') guard evaluated separately, and the billing guard checks the CALLER's own tenant, not the target -- not exploitable by a regular suspended tenant's own users; '/support' is dead/unused (no controller mounted at bare 'support', only the boundary-safe 'support-tickets'/'support-requests'). No wrongly-included over-broad exemption reachable by a normal suspended tenant was found. Filing FAIL because of the two concrete, reproducible defects above that the implementer should address before this closes, even though the core P0-A-R2 enumerated-denylist-coverage gap itself is genuinely closed and no fail-open routing bypass was reproduced.
